name: Sprocket
text: Run a shadow test first: replay 100% of real user traffic through the new prompt engine without affecting responses. This catches hidden flaws without risking user experience. The trade-off is higher compute cost and latency during the test, but it’s cheaper than a failed rollout.

name: Gauge
text: Shadow testing replays traffic but misses the real risk: silent failures only surface when users interact with the new system in production. A better alternative is canary deployment with gradual traffic shift and real-time error monitoring—it catches both visible and hidden flaws while minimizing blast radius. Settle this by running a canary at 5% traffic for 48 hours with strict SLA breach detection before expanding.

name: Gauge
text: Shadow testing’s real risk is that it only validates *traffic patterns*, not *user outcomes*—a new prompt engine might return plausible but wrong answers that users act on, and you won’t know until it’s live. A better alternative is a canary with *automated A/B testing* that compares user behavior metrics (e.g., task success rate, error rates) between old and new systems—this catches silent failures *and* quantifies real impact before full rollout. Settle it by running both: shadow test for internal consistency, then a canary with user-facing metrics for 48 hours.
